programs.name: 3-K
programs.plainLanguageName: Early education for three-year-olds
programs.summary: Free, full-day and high-quality education for New York City three-year-olds.
programs.eligibilityText:
All New York City families with children born in 2023 can apply for the upcoming school year. This includes children with disabilities or new English speakers.
Children do not need to be toilet trained to attend 3-K.
programs.requiredDocumentsText: View the pre-registration checklist to learn more about the documents you need to pre-register your child and accept their 3-K offer.

programs.name: Accelerated Study in Associate Programs
programs.plainLanguageName: Help earning your CUNY degree
programs.agency: The City University of New York (CUNY)
programs.summary: CUNY students can get financial, academic, and personal support to help them complete their associate degree.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for CUNY ASAP, you should:
· Apply and be accepted to a CUNY college that offers ASAP
· Be a New York City resident or eligible for in-state tuition
· Agree to enter into a full-time associate degree program in an ASAP-approved major
· Be proficient in Math and/or English (reading and writing)
· Have no more than 15 college credits and a minimum GPA of 2.0.

programs.name: Access-A-Ride Paratransit Service
programs.plainLanguageName: Public transportation for people with disabilities
programs.summary: Paratransit service for travel within NYC and nearby parts of Nassau and Westchester counties.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may qualify for Access-A-Ride if:
You have a disability that prevents you from using buses or subways for some or all of your trips.
Your needs match ADA requirements. You'll be asked about your ability to:
· Go up or down subway stairs
· Travel to a bus or subway station
· Get on, ride, and exit a bus or subway
· Navigate the bus or subway system on your own
You're temporarily unable to use public transit. This includes recovering from surgery, managing a long-term condition, or looking for paratransit services while visiting NYC.
programs.requiredDocumentsText: You will need medical documents that prove your transportation-related disability.

programs.name: Adult Protective Services
programs.plainLanguageName: Help for adults in danger of abuse, neglect or exploitation
programs.summary: Refer someone to APS if you suspect they are in danger of abuse, neglect, or exploitation.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for APS, you should be able to answer yes to the following questions:
· Are you 18 or older?
· Do you have a physical or mental disability?
· Are you unable to manage your own resources, carry out daily activities, or protect yourself from dangerous situations without help from others?
· Do you have no one else who is willing and able to help you responsibly?

programs.name: Affordable Broadband Act
programs.plainLanguageName: Low-cost plans for home internet
programs.summary: Get discounted home internet through the Affordable Broadband Act if you receive SNAP, Medicaid, or other benefits.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may qualify for low-cost home internet if someone in your household receives any of the following benefits:
· Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program
· Medicaid
· Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption
· Disability Rent Increase Exemption
· Affordability benefit from a utility, such as the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP)
· Free or reduced-priced lunch through the National School Lunch Program
Not enrolled in any qualifying programs? You may still qualify based on household income. Contact your internet provider for income limits.

programs.plainLanguageName: A year-round community centers for young people
programs.agency: NYC Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD)
populationServed: All New Yorkers regardless of legal status
programs.summary: School-based community centers serving youth ages 5-21 young people
programs.eligibilityText:
· Youth ages 5-21 who are enrolled in school can participate.
· Beacon also offers adult programs for people who are over 21 years old.

programs.plainLanguageName: Free internet for NYCHA residents

programs.summary: Students can get hands-on career training while finishing high school or their high school equivalency (HSE).
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible to apply for a New York City public high school, you must be able to answer yes to these questions:
· Are you a New York City resident?

programs.name: Cash Assistance
programs.plainLanguageName: Monthly cash help when you are in need
programs.summary: Cash assistance can help you pay rent, utilities, and other emergency expenses.
programs.eligibilityText:
This program looks at several things to decide if you are eligible. Some of them include:
· how much money you earn
· how much money you receive from benefits
· how many people live in your house
· resources like cash or a checking account
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
To apply for Cash Assistance you will need to prove the following:
· Your identity: such as a photo ID, drivers license, passport, naturalization certificate, or hospital records.
· Where you live: such as a statement from your landlord, current rent receipt, lease, or mortgage records.
· Your income (if any): such as a current pay stub, business records, current income tax return, or an Unemployment Insurance Benefit statement.
Check the Cash Assistance document guide to see what else you can use as proof.

programs.summary: Get help avoiding foreclosure, dealing with late mortgage payments, preventing scams, and more.

programs.name: Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit
programs.plainLanguageName: Tax credit to help pay for childcare or care for disabled dependents
programs.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP); Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
programs.summary: Get money back if you paid for childcare or care for disabled dependents while working or looking for work.
programs.eligibilityText:
To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements:
· You (and your spouse if filing a joint return) have earned income
· You paid for care so you could work (you must identify your care provider with their name, address, and tax ID or Social Security Number on your tax return)
· You're filing as single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or married filing jointly
Who counts as a dependent?
· A child under age 13 who you claim as a dependent, or
· Your spouse or dependent of any age who can't care for themselves due to a physical or mental disability and lives with you for more than half the year
If you qualify for the federal credit, you can also claim the New York State credit when you file your state taxes. The state credit works the same way as the federal credit.
You can get an additional NYC credit if you meet all of these requirements:
· You lived in NYC for all or part of 2025.
· You paid childcare expenses for at least one child under age four on December 31, 2025.
· Your federal adjusted gross income was $30,000 or less.
· You qualified for the New York State credit.
programs.requiredDocumentsText: You'll need documents like W-2s, receipts from your care provider, your care provider's tax ID or Social Security Number, and records showing how much you paid for care.

programs.name: Child Tax Credit
programs.plainLanguageName: Tax credit for families with children
programs.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP); Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
programs.summary: Claim the federal Child Tax Credit and the Empire State Child Tax Credit to get up to $3,200 per child under age four and up to $2,700 per child ages 4 to 16.
programs.eligibilityText:
To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements:
Filing status
Annual income limit
Single, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse
Up to $200,000
Married filing jointly
Up to $400,000
You must have:
· A child, stepchild, grandchild, foster child, adopted child, sibling, niece, or nephew under age 17
· A Social Security Number (SSN) or Adoption Tax Identification Number (ATIN) for yourself and your dependent(s)
· Lived with your dependent(s) for more than half the year in the US
· Claimed the dependent on your tax return (the dependent cannot provide more than half of their own financial support)
Important: Only one parent can claim a child for the CTC. If you share custody, talk with the other parent about who will claim your child to avoid filing issues.
Requirements for the Empire State Child Tax Credit
You qualify if you're a full-year New York State resident or are married to one, have a qualifying child, and meet one of these requirements:
· You claimed the federal CTC, or
· Your New York adjusted gross income is $75,000 or less (single/head of household), $110,000 or less (married filing jointly), or $55,000 or less (married filing separately)
Each child listed on your claim needs a valid SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).

· You are a U.S. citizen, noncitizen national, or qualified noncitizen.

· The death was attributed to COVID-19, as noted on the death certificate.

programs.name: CUNY Fatherhood Academy
programs.plainLanguageName: High school & college for young dads
programs.agency: The City University of New York (CUNY)
programs.summary: Education, employment, and parenting help for fathers ages 18 - 30.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for CUNY Fatherhood Academy, you should be able to answer yes to these questions.
For the high school equivalency AND college prep track:
· Do you live in New York City?
· Are you a father or an expecting father?
For the high school equivalency track only:
· Are you between 18 and 30 years old?
· Can you commit to a 16-week program for three days a week?
For the college prep track only:
· Are you between 18 and 30 years old?
· Do you have a high school diploma, HSE diploma, or GED?
· Do you have less than 12 college credits?
· Are you currently not enrolled in college?

programs.plainLanguageName: Academic support for CUNY students
programs.agency: The City University of New York (CUNY)
programs.summary: CUNY students can get help meeting CUNY's proficiency standards and preparing for college-level courses.
programs.eligibilityText:
You might be eligible for CUNY Start/Math Start if you can answer yes to these questions:
· Have you earned a high school or high school equivalency diploma?
· Have you completed all CUNY admissions requirements and accepted your offer to CUNY?
· Could you benefit from extra support in English and/or math based on your proficiency index scores?
· Are you able to commit to the program's academic schedule and its unique, student-centered instructional approach?
Specific colleges may have other eligibility criteria. Contact the CUNY Start program at your campus for more information.

programs.name: Disability Rent Increase Exemption
programs.plainLanguageName: Rent freeze for people with disabilities
programs.summary: A rent freeze program to help eligible New Yorkers stay in their home
programs.eligibilityText:
To qualify for DRIE, you'll need to meet basic requirements, live in certain types of apartments, and receive a qualifying disability benefit.
Basic requirements
· You're 18 years old or older
· Your name is on the lease
· Your household income is $50,000 or less per year
· You spend more than one-third of your monthly income on rent
Where you live
· Rent stabilized apartment
· Rent controlled apartment
· Mitchell-Lama development
· Limited Dividend development
· Redevelopment company development
· Housing Development Fund Company (HDFC) Cooperative development
· Section 213 Cooperative unit
· Rent-regulated hotel or single-room occupancy unit
Qualifying disability benefits
· Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
· Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
· Veterans Affairs (VA) disability pension or compensation
· Disability-related Medicaid
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
When you apply, have copies of these documents ready:
· Proof of identity and age: Government-issued ID (passport, driver's license, state ID)
· Proof of where you live: Current lease, recent rent receipt or payment confirmation
· Proof of income: Last year's tax return, W-2s, pay stubs, and benefit letters for all household members
· Proof of your disability benefit: Award letter from SSI, SSDI, VA, or Medicaid

programs.name: Disabled Homeowners' Exemption
programs.plainLanguageName: Property tax break for homeowners with disabilities
programs.summary: Lowered property tax for homeowners with disabilities who earn up to a certain income.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for DHE, you must meet these requirements:
· Own a one-, two-, or three-family home, condo, or coop apartment.
· All property owners are people with disabilities. However, if you own the property with a spouse or sibling, only one of you need to have a disability to qualify.
· You must live on the property as your primary residence.
· The combined income for all owners must be less than or equal to $58,399.
You may be eligible if your property is in a Housing Development Fund Corporation development and is in the Division of Alternative Management Program. Your property cannot be within a housing development controlled by a Limited Profit Housing Company, Mitchell-Lama, Limited Dividend Housing Company, or redevelopment company. Contact your property manager if you're not sure.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
To apply for DHE you will need to prove the following:
Your disability status: one of the following for an owner:
·
· Copy of Disability Award letter from the Social Security Administration
· Copy of Disability Award letter from the Railroad Retirement Board or the U.S Postal Service
· Copy of Certificate from the New York State Commission for the Blind, or a Veterans Administration letter stating that you are entitled to a veterans disability pension.
· Your income: copies of federal tax returns and additional forms (schedules) for all owners. If any owners do not file a tax return, provide proof of yearly earnings.
· Your deductions:
· Copies of receipts for your paid medical bills not covered by insurance for your income documentation year, OR
· Copy of your Schedule A

programs.summary: Cash help for people who can't pay an expense due to an unexpected situation or event.
programs.eligibilityText:

· income (earned and unearned)
· household size
· the reason for the need, like as losing a job
· available savings and resources
· affordability of housing
· disability
· a future plan to pay the expense moving forward
· citizenship or immigration status
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
HRA will request specific documents on a case by case basis. They may include:
· Birth certificate or Social Security Number and/or a photo ID for each adult in the household
· Proof of income for all members of your household
· Bills or letters from the landlord for monthly rent, and rent owed
· Copies of court orders
· Lease
After you give HRA the information it needs for your application, they will make a decision as soon as possible. HRA will send you a notice if they need more information or documents from you.

programs.summary: Help for parents and their children who have emotional, behavioral, or mental health challenges through peer-led programs.
programs.eligibilityText: Parents or caregivers of a child 0 to 24 years old who is at risk of or currently experiences emotional, behavioral or mental health challenges.

programs.name: Family Type Homes for Adults
programs.plainLanguageName: Homes for adults who cannot live alone
programs.agency: NYS Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS); NYC Human Resources Administration (HRA)
programs.summary: Supportive housing for adults who cannot live alone due to old age, developmental disabilities, or physical or mental health.
programs.eligibilityText:
You must meet these basic requirements:
· Be at least 18 years old
· Need help with daily living tasks (you can't live independently without support)
· Have a developmental disability, physical disability, cognitive impairment, or mental illness
If you have certain diagnoses, you also need to:
· Attend a day treatment program (if you've been diagnosed with a developmental disability or mental illness)
· Be at least five years clean or sober (if you have a history of substance abuse)
You won't qualify for FTHAs if you:
· Are wheelchair-bound or bed-ridden
· Have a history of substance abuse (unless you're five years clean or sober)
· Have difficulties following medication and treatment plans
· Have a history of arson
· Have a history of verbal or abusive behavior
· Have been incarcerated

programs.plainLanguageName: Services for people with HIV or AIDS
programs.summary: HASA helps people living with HIV or AIDS get health care and other public benefits.
programs.eligibilityText: To be eligible for HASA, you must have been diagnosed with HIV or with AIDS, as defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). You do not need to have symptoms to be eligible.

programs.name: Home Care Services Program
programs.plainLanguageName: Long-term care at home
programs.summary: Seniors and people with disabilities can receive health care in their home.
programs.eligibilityText: Home care programs have different eligibility requirements, but they all require that you must be eligible for Medicaid.

· your fuel or utility expenses: such as a recent bill or statement from your landlord stating that utilities are included in your rent.
· disability status: if someone in your household has a disability.

programs.name: Homebase
programs.plainLanguageName: Services to help you keep your housing
populationServed: All New Yorkers regardless of legal status
programs.summary: If you're at risk of homelessness, Homebase offers support to stay out of shelter and remain stably housed.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may be eligible for Homebase services if you:
· Live in one of the five boroughs of NYC
· May be soon at risk of entering the NYC shelter system
· Want to remain stably housed in your community
If you think you need Homebase services, contact a local office so they can review your specific situation and offer support. Even if you are not eligible, Homebase can help you find resources that might be helpful.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
These are the documents you need to bring on your first appointment. If you don't have all of these documents, Homebase can still assess your case and help.
· ID for all household members 18 years or older
· Proof of income/employment for every working member of the household (recent paystubs dated within 30 days of Homebase appointment)
· If you have an active Cash Assistance (CA) case, bring a CA Budget Letter or Welfare Management System (WMS) printout dated within 30 days
· Unemployment letter
· Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability (SSD) Award Letter, dated within the last year
· Copy of lease or written rental agreement
· Rental Assistance referral, certificate, voucher, or award letter
· Rent demand, landlord letter, or court documents
· Light, gas, and telephone bill

programs.name: Homeless Intake Shelters & Drop-In Centers
programs.plainLanguageName: Adult and family shelters and drop-in housing services
programs.summary: If you're experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis, you can apply for shelter or get help finding stable housing.
programs.eligibilityText: Visit an intake center to apply for shelter and discuss your eligibility. Drop-in centers are open to everyone.

programs.eligibilityText: All New Yorkers ages 10 and up qualify.

programs.summary: Jobs Plus is an employment program that helps NYCHA residents find employment and increase their earnings.
programs.eligibilityText: NYCHA residents who are old enough to work and live in one of the 27 developments served can enroll in Jobs-Plus.

programs.plainLanguageName: Free early childhood education for children of student-parents
programs.summary: Student-parents can get free early childhood education for their children ages 6 weeks to 4 years.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may be eligible for LYFE if you answer yes to the following questions:
· Are you enrolled in or eligible to enroll inan NYC Department of Education school or program?
· Is your child between 6 weeks and 4 years old, and not age-eligible for Pre-K for All?
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
· Proof of your child's age
· A current copy of your child's immunization records
· A Child & Adolescent Health Examination Form for your child

programs.name: Medicaid
programs.plainLanguageName: Free health insurance for low-income residents
programs.summary: Covers doctor and clinic visits, regular exams, immunizations, and other health needs.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may qualify for Medicaid if you:
· Live in New York State
· Are a U.S. citizen or meet immigration status requirements
· Meet income limits for your age group and household size
Check your income limit:
· Children under age 1
· Children ages 1-18
· Ages 19-20 living with your parents
· Pregnant people
· Adults under age 65, caretakers, and parents
· Adults ages 65 and older, people with a disability or visual impairment
If your income is too high for Medicaid, you could still qualify through the Medicaid Excess Income Program.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
You'll need to show proof of:
· Identity and date of birth (a passport, driver's license, or birth certificate)
· U.S. citizenship or immigration status
· Your current home address (a lease, utility bills, or a government ID card with address)
· Your income for the past four weeks (paystubs, signed and dated letter from your employer, benefits letters)
You may also need to provide:
· Proof of resources such as bank statements (required if you're 65 or older or have a disability)
· Current health insurance information, if you have it
· Medical bills from the past three months, if you're applying for retroactive coverage

programs.summary: Reduced MTA fares are available for anyone 65+ or with a qualifying disability.
programs.eligibilityText:
You qualify if any of the following apply:
· Are 65 or older
· Receive Medicare benefits for any reason other than age
· Have a serious mental illness and receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
· Have blindness
· Have deafness or hearing loss
· Have an ambulatory, cognitive, or other physical disability

· Driver's license from any state
· Passport from any country
· IDNYC

programs.name: National Flood Insurance Program
programs.plainLanguageName: Flood insurance
programs.summary: Flood insurance covers damage to your home and belongings.
programs.eligibilityText: Anyone in NYC can buy flood insurance.

programs.name: Newborn Home Visiting Program
programs.plainLanguageName: Home visits for first-time parents
programs.agency: NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
programs.summary: First-time parents can get support from a health professional to help with breastfeeding, health and safety tips, and connect to community resources.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for this program, you should be a first-time parent who lives in one of these neighborhoods.
You may also be eligible if you are a parent with a baby less than 3 months old and who:
· lives in a NYCHA development in one of these neighborhoods.
· currently gets help from the Administration for Children's Services (ACS).
· lives in a Department of Homeless Services (DHS) shelter.

programs.name: NYC 988
programs.plainLanguageName: Talk, text, or chat for mental health help
programs.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
programs.summary: Free and private talk, text, or chat mental health services available any time for you or someone you care about.
programs.eligibilityText: NYC 988 doesn't ask about immigration status.

programs.name: NYC Care
programs.plainLanguageName: No cost or low-cost healthcare
programs.summary: Comprehensive healthcare for all NYC residents, regardless of income or immigration status.
programs.eligibilityText:
You qualify for NYC Care if you:
· Live in NYC (any of the five boroughs)
· Don't have health insurance from your employer
· Don't qualify for any health insurance plan available in New York State
· Can't afford health insurance based on government guidelines
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
You will need proof of:
· Identification
· New York City residency
· Household income
· Household size
Patients who have already been screened for insurance through the NYS of Health Marketplace can bring a printout of the results of the determination and will not need additional documentation.
If you are unable to provide the required documents, a counselor still may be able to help you enroll. Call 646-NYC-CARE (646-692-2273) for more information.

programs.name: NYC Child Care Connect
programs.plainLanguageName: Find a licensed child care program
programs.agency: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
programs.summary: An online resource that helps you find and stay informed about a child care program in your community.

programs.name: NYC Family Justice Centers
programs.plainLanguageName: Help for survivors of domestic and gender-based violence
programs.agency: NYC Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV)
programs.summary: Counseling and services are available in all boroughs for survivors of domestic, and gender-based violence.
programs.eligibilityText: People of any age, income, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, or language spoken are welcome at FJCs.

programs.name: NYC Ferry Discount Program
programs.plainLanguageName: Discounted one-way tickets for NYC Ferry
programs.agency: New York City Economic Development Corporation
programs.summary: For seniors 65 and older, people with disabilities, high school students, and Fair Fares NYC participants.
programs.eligibilityText:
Get discounted one-way ferry tickets if you're:
· 65 or older
· A person with a disability
· A NYC high school student
· A Fair Fares NYC participant

programs.name: NYC Financial Empowerment Centers
programs.plainLanguageName: Free financial counseling
programs.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
programs.summary: Get help with managing your money and improving your financial health.
programs.eligibilityText: You qualify for free counseling if you're at least age 18 and live or work in NYC.

programs.name: NYC Free Tax Prep
programs.plainLanguageName: Free tax prep services
programs.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
programs.summary: Free tax prep services are available at over 140 locations across NYC that can help you file in-person, online, or over the phone
programs.eligibilityText:
For tax year 2025, youre eligible for NYC Free Tax Prep if you earned:
· $97,000 or less in 2025 and have qualifying children or dependents
· $68,000 or less in 2025 and do not have qualifying children or dependents
programs.requiredDocumentsText: You'll need specific documents to file your taxes, like W-2s, receipts, and ID.

programs.name: NYC Housing Connect
programs.plainLanguageName: Affordable housing lotteries
programs.agency: NYC Housing Preservation and Development (HPD); NYC Housing Development Corporation (HDC)
programs.summary: An online portal where you can apply to rent or buy an affordable unit or home.
programs.eligibilityText:
Each lottery has different income requirements based on your household size. Check the requirements on
NYC Housing Connect
before you apply.
Ready to Rent
offers free one-on-one financial counseling and help with applications. Some lotteries give priority to NYC residents who have a disability, are seniors, or live in the same neighborhood.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
If your lottery application gets selected, you may need to provide:
· Proof of income (paystubs, W-2 forms, benefits statements)
· Asset information (bank or investment statements)
· Rent payment history or credit check
· IDs and birth certificates for household members
See the full document list on NYC Housing Connect.

programs.name: NYC Ladders for Leaders
programs.plainLanguageName: Internships for high school and college students
programs.agency: NYC Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD)
programs.summary: High school and college students can participate in paid summer internships at top New York City companies, non-profits, and government agencies.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may be eligible if you can answer yes to these questions.
· Do you live in New York City?
· Are you currently enrolled in high school or college?
· Are you between 16 - 22 years old?
· Do you have previous work experience (even as a volunteer)?
· Do you have a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.00?
· If you are under 18 years old, do you have your working papers?

· Benefit card
· NYS Driver license/learner's permit
· Non-citizen (alien) registration card
· U.S. Passport

· Home utility bill
· Lease, mortgage, or deed
· Cable bill (must have phone service listed)
· Official mail from a Federal, State or City Agency

In addition, all youth will need to provide one of the following:

· Official school transcript
· NYS Driver license/learner's permit
· Voters registration card
· U.S. military card/draft record

· Official college transcript
· Unofficial college transcript with a copy of your college ID

· U.S. Birth Certificate

· Official letter from Social Services (Must include applicants name, Benefit #, and date)
If not supported by Public Assistance:
· Two (2) consecutive pay stubs dated within the last six months (Must include payee name, and gross income)
· 2021 W-2 form and one (1) pay stub dated within the last six months
· Current Pension Award letter
· Current SSA Award letter
· Unemployment Benefit Document dated within the last six months
· If self-employed, 2021 Tax Return including Schedule C or E (if receiving rental income)
Proof of social security number
· Social Security Card
Proof of Selective Service registration (for males 18 and older)
One of the following:
· Record of online registration (www.sss.gov)
· Online receipt
Proof of disability status (if applicable)
One of the following:
· Proof of Social Security Disability or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
· Statement from medical professional
· Other official documentation for ACS, HRA, your school stating you have a disability

programs.summary: Free service to help older adults and people with disabilities remain independent at home and in their community.

· Caregivers of older adults and parents of children with a disability.
· Professional service providers working with someone in need of long term services and supports.

· official photo ID

programs.name: NYS Paid Family Leave
programs.plainLanguageName: Paid time off to care for family
programs.summary: Up to 12 weeks of paid time off to care for a new child, sick family member, and other situations.
programs.eligibilityText:
You may be able to take Paid Family Leave if you:
· Are a resident of New York State.
· Work for a private employer in New York State or for a public employer who has opted in.
· Some workers aren't eligible for PFL Learn more about what kinds of workers are eligible.
· If youre not sure if you're covered for PFL, speak to your employer.
· Meet the time-worked requirements before taking Paid Family Leave:
· Full-time employees who regularly work 20 or more hours/week can take PFL after working 26 consecutive weeks.
· Part-time employees who regularly work less than 20 hours/week can take PFL after working 175 days. These days don't need to be consecutive.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
You'll need different documents depending on your situation. Check the links below for the documents that you'll need.
· Bonding leave for:
· the birth of a child
· the adoption of a child
· fostering a child
· Family Care
· Military Family Support
· New Paid Leave for COVID-19
In general, you'll need to prove your identity, family relationship, address, and income.
You'll also need to provide proof of a qualifying event to file a PFL claim.

· Be actively seeking work and able to start a job immediately
· Be authorized to work in the US (and have been authorized when you lost your job)
You'll also need to:
· Keep a written record of your job search activities each week (you can use the JobZone work search tool)
· Attend required appointments at your local Career Center
· Meet minimum earnings requirements (see how much you need to have earned)
programs.requiredDocumentsText:

Your personal information
· Full name, phone number, and mailing address
· Social Security Number
· Driver's license, state ID, or employment authorization number (if you're not a US citizen)
· Bank account number and routing number
Information about your past jobs (last 18 months)
· Your employer's legal name and address
· Your employer's Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or New York State registration number (you can find this on your W-2 or employment record)
· Your start and end dates
· Your wage details
· If you served in the military in the last 18 months, you'll also need your DD214

· Are age 65 or older

programs.summary: Lowered property taxes for senior homeowners who earn up to a certain income.
programs.eligibilityText:
To be eligible for SCHE, you must meet these requirements:
· Own a one-, two-, or three-family home, condo, or coop apartment.
· All owners of the property are 65 or older. However, if you own the property with a spouse or sibling, only one of you need to be 65 or older.
· All owners must live on the property as the primary residence.
· The combined income for all owners must be less than or equal to $58,399.
· You must own the property for at least 12 consecutive months before the date of filing for the exemption. This is not a requirement if you got the exemption on a property that you owned before.
programs.requiredDocumentsText:
To apply for SCHE you will need to prove the following:
· Your age: you need a copy of a government-issued ID
· Your income: copies of federal tax returns and additional forms (schedules) for all owners. If any owners do not file a tax return, provide proof of yearly earnings.
· Your deductions:
· Copies of receipts for your paid medical bills not covered by insurance for your income documentation year, OR
· Copy of your Schedule A
· Depending on your application, you may need a trust agreement, will, or other legal documents.

· Do you spend more than one-third of your monthly income on rent?

· a rent controlled apartment
· a rent regulated hotel or single room occupancy unit
· a Mitchell-Lama development
· a Limited Dividend Housing Company development
· a Redevelopment Company development
· a Housing Development Fund Company development

· Who you are (and your age)

· Income - This includes your income and the income of all household members who lived in your apartment for the year before you submit your application.

· Is the property your primary residence?
· Are you a veteran who served in the US armed forces during one of the following conflicts?
